concept.name: POV order
concept.definition: An algorithmic execution order that targets a fixed percentage of the market's traded volume: the algo speeds up when market volume rises and slows when it falls, so the order continuously participates at the specified rate until complete.
concept.intuition: POV is 'stay a constant fraction of the flow' - if you ask for 10% of volume, the algo keeps buying (or selling) so that you are roughly one tenth of everything that prints.
concept.mechanics: The algo watches real-time volume and submits child orders to keep cumulative participation near the target rate (typically user-set between 1% and 50%), within start/end times and optionally with a 'never take liquidity' constraint that restricts it to passive fills at the cost of completion risk.
concept.formula: Participation rate = cumulative own executed volume / cumulative market volume over the same window; the algo steers this toward the target percentage.
concept.failure_modes: Completion time is unbounded: in a dead market the order may never finish, while a volume surge forces aggressive catch-up trading with elevated impact. A fixed participation rate also becomes predictable and can be gamed by other participants watching the flow.
concept.misconceptions: POV does not cap the order's share of daily volume in advance - it tracks volume as it happens, so total execution time and end-time price exposure are unknown when the order is placed. Nor does a low participation rate guarantee low impact.
concept.example: You work a 300,000-share sell at a 10% POV target; in an hour when 500,000 shares trade, the algo sells about 50,000, then throttles back when volume dries up.

citations.source: Interactive Brokers TWS API: IB Algorithms
